Issued at 222 AM MST Sat Nov 28 2026

We are listening to 70s and 80s music this morning at the 
humble Riverton weather abode. And one of my favorite artists 
from this time is David Bowie. And one of his best known songs 
remains me of what will happen east of the Divide this morning,
especially when compared to most of November. And the song is 
"Changes." It has been relatively snow free in central Wyoming. 
Casper is now on the 3rd latest day with an inch of snow, tying 
2nd today. Lander, which has records dating back to 1896, is 
the sixth latest. And we are tied for 2nd latest at Riverton. 
However, some of this will end today. We have two main concerns 
today, snow and wind. We will be talking about the impacts of 
each of these individually. And, what cha-cha-cha Changes this 
system will bring.

SNOW...Snow continues across much of western Wyoming at this 
time, with radar showing a particularly heavy area of snow 
approaching from the west as I write this around 1:30 am this 
morning. The cold front hasn't passed this area yet, with 700 
millibar temperatures remaining between around minus 1 to minus 
3 Celsius. As a result, snow levels are still 7000 feet or 
above for the most part. As a result, the valleys are largely 
rain. The chance of 3 inches or more of snow in these locations 
is generally less than 1 out of 10. The mountains will still see
heavy snow though, and we will continue the warnings for now. 
The one I have the most concern about is the Upper Green 
Foothills. Much of the area, especially around Pinedale, will 
not see warning level amounts of snow. The warning is more for 
places like Bondurant. In the west, the heaviest snow should be 
over by sunrise as the cold front and trough axis from the 
system move through, but light snow showers may linger for a 
while after. The warning could be cancelled early, but we will 
cross that bridge when we get to it. Most of the higher 
elevations of the west have at least a 4 out of 5 chance of an 
additional 6 inches of snow, with the highest elevations having 
a 1 out of 2 chance of over a foot of additional snow.

Now we move east of the Divide. There continues to be a bit 
more uncertainty here. Colder air is now moving in from the 
north. The Buffalo airport has already changed to snow and it is
snowing moderately there right now. The front will continue 
advancing southward through the morning, reaching the 
Continental Divide shortly after sunrise. The concerns here are 
the same as before. A lot of snow would be frontal and also of 
the banded variety. In addition, the models continue to have 
different ideas on the placement of the heaviest snow. However, 
we did make a few changes. There is decent model agreement in 
showing a greater than 3 out of 5 chance of 3 inches of snow or 
more across much of Natrona County as well as western Johnson 
County, this includes portions of Interstate 25. This, combined 
with the wind we will talk about below, will likely make for 
some difficult travel today into early afternoon. So, we have 
hoisted a Winter Weather Advisory for Johnson and Natrona 
Counties through 11 am and 2 pm, respectively. Snow amounts 
will be somewhat elevation dependent here. In the lower 
elevations, the heaviest snow would fall in areas that are 
slightly higher, like US-20/26 in western Natrona County. The 
least snow may end up being in Casper itself, with the elevation
somewhat lower. Elsewhere, amounts should be less, generally 2 
inches or less. However, there is the chance of snow squalls, in
places like the Wind River Basin, the Lander Foothills and 
maybe even Sweetwater County that could bring locally heavier 
amounts. This is far from certain though, so this would be best 
handled with short fuse statements. The maximum impacts are 
expected from now through noon, with snow then tapering off and 
ending for all areas by sunset as the front and system move away
to the east.

WIND...Wind is starting to increase across portions of the 
area. However, the strongest wind is expected between 5 am and 
noon as the cold front and trough advance across the area. It is
a decent set up for high wind in portions of the area. The 
trough and cold front will provide good mixing across the area. 
The strongest wind is expected in southern Wyoming, where 700 
millibar winds of 50 to 60 knots may mix to the surface. 
Probabilistic guidance shows at least a 1 in 2 chance of wind 
gusts over 55 mph through noon across much of Sweetwater County.
So, we hoisted a High Wind Warning from Rock Springs and 
eastward through 11 am, when wind turns northeast, ending the 
high wind threat. We also left the High Wind Warning in effect 
for the Green Mountains and Rattlesnake Range, although this 
area is north of the strongest mid level wind and the threat may
be a bit lower. We also thought about adding Rock Springs and 
Green River to the warning, but the core of the strongest wind 
would likely remain south of Interstate 80
